newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, LOOKS TO BUYING LATER.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, LOOKS TO BUYING LATER.

text.p: The Singapore rubber exchange was quiet by midday on Thursday with the trade waiting for the afternoon session in the hope that buyers will come into the market, dealers said.
"It was practically untraded this morning. It's a waiting game, but we should see some business done this afternoon as usual," a dealer said.
The trader said the market was hoping for further buying by Michelin, which was said to have bought some nearby cargoes of RSS3 rubber yesterday as part of its weekly buying programme.
Some dealers were also hopeful that Bridgestone will be in the market later in the day.
One trader said a solitary deal for prompt RSS1 rubber was registered in the morning, but the transaction was probably concluded on Wednesday.
"I don't think that deal was done by the Japanese trade house today," a dealer said.

At 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 93.75 U.S. cents a kg from 94.00 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 137.00-139.00 Singapore cents (93-94 U.S. cents) a kg from 137.25 cents. -- (S$1.47 = US$1) - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
